summary: Correct “seized to exist” to “ceased to exist”.
rationale: The English construction is “ceased to exist”. The Turoyo tlo and the edition’s “ist verschwunden” confirm cessation, not seizure.

summary: Preserve glossary stem I for the integrated Arabic X loan; Arabic morphology does not justify renaming the Turoyo stem. Active generic users can be translated by an English construction with the used object as subject (Lahdo The mill/1).
Infectum-wa is newly documented for cattle use and a wooden trough. The latter explicitly contrasts former use with current continued use, without a change of lexical meaning.

At MAC Ishaq Material culture/82, čmənto is an unmarked function/material complement after a suffixed theme. Record the government pattern under existing gebrauchen, not as a numbered sense solely for a material participant.

The inherited Detransitive Infectum at 12/20 is the one clear supplied finite Detransitive. məstaʕmalwa at Material culture/64 lacks sufficient evidence to choose Preterit-wa, Part. Pass. plus wa, or a reduced finite pattern.
Using one’s freedom remains a transparent abstract-object use, already present in the Imperativ; no new idiom is established.
Retain glossary stem I for the integrated Arabic X loan; no stem X is introduced. Jan adds clear active Preterit l-agent forms and first-person/plural-agent contrasts absent after round 1.
Round 1 already added Infectum-wa; reader claims of an absent box are stale. This round fills its remaining three slots with fuel, second-person implements and medicine/purpose contexts.
The mitəstaʕməl-series encodes Detransitive themes (terms, tax money), whereas agentive use may have a nonhuman institution as subject. English used wording does not determine the voice.

stəʕmolo is a learned use noun in language-policy exposition, with d-genitive theme and b-domain. Nomen Actionis is conservative filing; ordinary Infinitiv remains to be elicited. The unprefixed predicative məstaʕməl book description does not settle the finite Detransitive paradigm.
Resolve məstaʕmalwa at MAC Ishaq Material culture/64: which glossary box is supported by its morphology? Withhold a new-box proposal pending confirmation.
Check 94/4 against the edition: supplied koməstaʕmele differs from inherited ko-məstaʕme-la. Do not silently harmonise patient agreement.
Why does 53/128 have ḥurriyayḏux while addressing the sister? Preserve both source and inherited possessive forms.
Confirm whether social ʕam-contact in 95/34 is a conventional independent use. Only this one nonsexual reciprocal attestation is supplied.
All Jan quotations use supplied machine English. Obtain editorial translations, especially the rhetorical question at Jan 4.I/478, whose Turoyo has no printed question mark.
Jan 1.17/880: does the government observe the festival, employ the festival institution, or use its designation? A distinct celebrate sense is withheld.
Confirm Nomen Actionis stəʕmolo versus a regular Infinitiv, and predicative məstaʕməl at Jan 4.I/242 versus an Arabic loan adjective or reduced Detransitive.
Confirm contraction in məstaʕmeli/məstaʕməli and məstaʕmalxu. Source spellings retained; no consonants restored.
Ordinary use takes mills, houses, animals, tools, words, freedom and foodstuffs as themes. No separate lexical senses are needed for these participants or for using a substance as cement.

Authority, letters, calendars, language, medicines, tools, fuel, money and forces are used themes. Exercise of authority parallels the inherited freedom Imperativ; no separate light-verb idiom is needed. Festival observance is provisional, not established as a distinct sense.
